summary: Resume interrupted evidence GC deletions from a durable plan before planning another run

replay.detail: An opt-in local journal retains the frozen deletion plan. A later invocation re-confirms its log hook and completes remaining remote and local operations without fetching or verifying the records again. There are no graph replay changes. Protection-kept groups finish as reported outcomes, allowing the next run to plan fresh work; other failures retain the journal.

schema.detail: Adds a versioned, checksummed local journal selected with --resume-state. Its plan file includes an operation_id in plan_sha256 so identical later plans have distinct GC markers. Evidence record and signed log line formats do not change. The existing gc-pending mapping and expiration rule are unchanged.

rules.detail: Retention, signer trust, whole-group deletion and remote protection are unchanged. Every resumed hook must publish through the existing ancestry check and lease. Remote operations additionally require the original object IDs.

compatibility.detail: The new GC wrapper enables the optional resume journal and nonblocking log-lock flag. Commands without the resume flags retain their interface. Older log readers tolerate the unchanged GC lines; the resumed plan-file field is additive. Older GC executables do not understand the new flags, so revert the wrapper with them only after finishing any outstanding plan.

downtime.detail: No daemon downtime or service deadline increase. A busy publisher makes the GC hook refuse promptly. The next scheduled run can finish the saved plan after a timeout or interruption. A collision with a pull can defer deletion until the next daily invocation; no hook retry loop is added.

manual.detail: Install the updated evidence-gc-timer wrapper to enable resumable timer runs. Keep paused GC paused until the remaining pending-state fix is installed and an operator explicitly releases the pause. No installed state or service is changed by this code update.

recovery.detail: Keep pending-plan.json until completion; do not edit or discard it to bypass a refusal. Remote refs already gone and a local transaction already committed are safe to replay. A changed ref, remote, repository, hook, invalid journal or failed publication refuses further deletion. Failed publication preserves pending names and copies so a pull does not re-verify the records. Finish an outstanding journal with the new tool before downgrading. A failed publication may leave a signed local GC commit that an intervening pull publishes while copies stay retained; finish the journal to converge, or complete a later successful GC run for commands without a journal.
